correctness.rationale: Starting from Wang Prop.3.17, put P=prod_i a_i, q_I=prod_{i not in I}a_i, S_I=sum_{i in I}a_i. Its term equals S_I/P+(|I|-3)/q_I. For full I=A of size n+1, theta_A=S/P+n-2. For proper admissible I (|I|>=4), all positive weights give S_I<S, |I|<=n, q_I>=1, so theta_I <= S_I/P+n-3 < theta_A. Thus the full stratum uniquely maximizes for n>=3, yielding global hyperbolicity at the same strict m>n-2+S/P threshold as the off-boundary Prop.3.11. For P(1,1,2,3,5), n=4, P=30, S=12, threshold 12/5, so integral m>=3. Uses Wang hypotheses and sufficiency only; not claiming necessity or nonisolated singularity extension.
residual_risks: The proof of numeric maximization is elementary; it is valued only for the real global-geometric consequence, not as a novel inequality technique.
The conclusion must not be read as necessity or optimality of actual hyperbolicity degree for all weights.
Unindexed equivalent simplifications in other sources remain possible.
